purpose: Unpublished replacements; real representative test cases, linked repair/retest evidence and calibrated assessment remain required.

module_patch.subtitle: Test meaning, coverage and repaired behavior
module_patch.description: Interpret quality signals, verify expected values and demonstrate a source-supported repair with new execution and regression evidence.
objectives: Explain what quality scores and repeated results do and do not establish
Build representative cases with source-checked expectations
Preserve a failure, saved repair and linked retest without hiding coverage gaps
tips: Workflow validation can grade historical runs; execute the changed revision first.
Skipped fields and unavailable checks leave evidence gaps.
A high score describes measured conditions, not every future answer.

replacements.title: Test what the result needs to prove
replacements.objective: Separate correct structure, repeatability and source-supported meaning.
replacements.content:
A workflow can return well-formed output and still extract the wrong amount, omit a qualification or invent a deadline. Validation needs an explicit account of what correct output means for the intended use.

Check completeness, structure and meaning separately. A nonempty budget field establishes presence. A numeric format establishes shape. Neither establishes that the value is the full project budget rather than one year's request. That requires comparison with the relevant source and the field's definition.

Consistency measures agreement across repeated results. A workflow that returns the same wrong value every time can be highly consistent. Extraction accuracy compares results with saved expected values; those expectations must first be checked against the source. An incorrect expected value can reward an incorrect extraction.

Workflow checks can use a model evaluator to judge saved output and supplied source context. Treat its explanations as reviewable judgments, not independent proof. Inspect decisive source passages, intermediate results and any unavailable or skipped checks. A technical inability to evaluate is not a demonstrated pass or a learner failure.

**Practice:** A result is valid JSON and repeats the same budget three times. Identify what remains unknown before using that budget.

knowledge_check.question: A budget value is identical in three runs. What has that established?

options.text: The budget is correct.
options.explanation: Agreement does not establish which source amount the field should contain.

options.text: The observed runs agree; accuracy still needs a checked expected value and source.
options.explanation: Repeatability and source accuracy answer different questions.

options.text: The current result needs no further review.
options.explanation: Structure and repetition do not prove meaning or suitability.

replacements.title: Build checks that expose meaningful failures
replacements.objective: Choose representative cases and source-checked expectations rather than chasing a test count.
replacements.content:
Begin with the decisions the workflow supports and the errors that would matter. Turn those risks into specific checks with a stated input, expected behavior and evidence. "The report looks good" is too vague; "the total uses the full project period and preserves the currency" can expose a concrete error.

Use representative inputs that differ in the ways the workflow will encounter: layout, terminology, length, missing fields and ambiguous values. Include a difficult case, an absent value and an ordinary case. Do not invent a value to fill a missing-field test. State the allowed missing or unresolved behavior explicitly.

For known-answer cases, verify expected values in the source before saving them. An automatically proposed answer is a draft. Include the relevant passage and interpretation, such as the difference between an annual amount and a total award. A required field can legitimately be unresolved when the source does not establish it; the workflow should expose that limitation.

Keep some representative cases separate from the examples used to tune prompts. After a repair, test those held-out cases as well as the original failure. Repeatedly tuning against the same easy examples can improve their score without improving general use.

A larger test count can improve coverage only if the cases exercise meaningful differences. The scoring system's sample-size adjustment is not a certificate that three cases cover your domain. Plan execution cost and repetitions around the uncertainty you need to investigate.

**Practice:** Design one normal case, one ambiguous-amount case and one missing-value case. Explain the different failure each would detect.

knowledge_check.question: Which addition most improves a budget extractor test set?

options.text: Three copies of the same easy document.
options.explanation: Duplicate cases add little evidence about different failure modes.

options.text: Different layouts and an ambiguous annual-versus-total amount, with source-checked expectations.
options.explanation: Representative differences test the interpretation that matters.

options.text: The model's latest outputs saved as expected values without review.
options.explanation: That can turn the same mistake into the supposed correct answer.

replacements.title: Run, inspect, repair and validate again
replacements.objective: Preserve linked before-and-after execution and validation evidence.
replacements.content:
Use the assigned workflow and source documents for this course version. Keep the saved workflow revision, model/configuration, source identities and execution results linked to the validation record.

1. Define checks for the intended fields, meaning and unresolved cases. In the workflow editor's Validate area, review generated suggestions and save a plan that actually matches the workflow.
2. Check that the saved plan refers to the current fields and steps. Resolve stale-plan warnings before interpreting a grade as evidence about the current design.
3. Execute the saved workflow on the intended inputs and wait for its actual result. Inspect the source selection and intermediate outputs, including warnings or errors.
4. Run validation and inspect which completed executions it assessed. The current workflow validator grades recent completed runs; pressing validation alone does not execute your edited workflow on new inputs.
5. Read individual checks, skipped checks, source support and aggregate results. An old completed run, a binary output that could not be checked as text or a missing result cannot prove the repaired workflow passed.
6. For a substantive failure, identify its cause, save a bounded repair, then execute that revision again. Revalidate the new result and inspect any older results included in the comparison.
7. Preserve the original failure, the change and the linked retest. Include representative regression cases so fixing one field does not hide a new failure elsewhere.

**Practice:** Explain how you would distinguish a passing validation of yesterday's run from evidence that today's saved repair worked.

knowledge_check.question: You changed a prompt and then validated without executing again. What is missing?

options.text: A new execution of the saved revision on the intended input and validation tied to that result.
options.explanation: Validation of historical output cannot establish how the edited workflow behaves.

options.text: A more confident explanation from chat.
options.explanation: An explanation does not produce the missing execution evidence.

options.text: Nothing; validation always runs the changed workflow.
options.explanation: The workflow validator can grade recent completed runs rather than executing a new one.

replacements.title: Recheck after changes and preserve the comparison
replacements.objective: Use validation as an active regression practice with clear evidence limits.
replacements.content:
A saved validation plan describes checks; it does not by itself enforce them on every future execution. A green historical score remains evidence about the measured inputs, saved results and conditions of that validation.

Recheck after changing field meaning, source selection, prompts, workflow structure, extraction strategy or model configuration. A new document family may also require new cases even when the workflow is unchanged. Keep the old failure and run identity so a later improvement can be traced to an actual change.

Use the first failing case to diagnose the problem. Inspect where the wrong value entered the chain and whether the test itself is justified. Do not weaken a correct check merely to restore a green score. If the expected answer was wrong, correct it with source evidence and record why the evaluation changed.

Rerun both the original failing case and other representative cases after the repair. Check that downstream reports retain uncertainty and that previously correct fields remain correct. Separate changes to the workflow from changes to the test set when explaining a score difference.

Quality history, age indicators and regression alerts can direct attention to measured changes. Their presence depends on actual validation records and configured monitoring. An absence of alerts does not establish that every current result has been checked. Review the current run before relying on it.

**Practice:** A score rises after two difficult cases are removed. Explain why that alone is not evidence of a better workflow.

knowledge_check.question: A saved validation plan has passed before. What protects a changed workflow?

options.text: Assuming the previous pass applies to the new revision.
options.explanation: The previous result measured earlier conditions.

options.text: Executing and evaluating the changed revision on the failure and representative regression cases.
options.explanation: The comparison needs actual new evidence and useful coverage.

options.text: Deleting difficult cases until the score recovers.
options.explanation: That can hide the failure rather than repair it.

replacements.title: Trace an annual-versus-total budget failure
replacements.objective: Diagnose a source interpretation error and demonstrate its repair without inventing run history.
replacements.content:
Consider an illustrative proposal with a first-year request of 178,000 and a full project request of 485,000 in the same currency. These numbers describe this teaching example; they are not verified answers for your assigned document.

A field labeled "Budget" returns 178,000. The output is nonempty and numeric, and repeated extractions agree. Those checks pass while the intended full-project amount is wrong. The decisive test compares the field with the source-supported total and its period.

A useful plan checks distinct properties: the amount matches the intended total, the currency and period remain attached, the source reference supports that interpretation, required unresolved values remain visible, and the downstream narrative preserves the reviewed data. Do not substitute a fixed check count for coverage of the actual requirements.

Trace the failure to the extraction definition or supplied context. A possible repair is to define "Total project request across the full project period" and explicitly distinguish it from the first-year amount. Inspect the saved definition and run it again. A better label is a hypothesis about the repair until the new output is measured.

Compare the original failure with the new execution and evaluation. Use another document where the total is missing or the annual and full-period amounts are arranged differently. Check that the new prompt does not now invent a total or damage another field. Keep any remaining limitation in the result.

**Practice:** Write the failing check, proposed repair and evidence needed to establish that the repair worked. Do not report a successful run until it exists.

knowledge_check.question: The illustrative extractor returns 178,000 consistently instead of the full-period 485,000. What should change?

options.text: The expected total, so the consistent answer passes.
options.explanation: A correct source-checked expectation should not be weakened to match a mistake.

options.text: Clarify the intended field and context, then execute and test the repair with regression cases.
options.explanation: The repair must establish the correct meaning and preserve other behavior.

options.text: Only the output format.
options.explanation: Formatting cannot establish which amount is semantically correct.

replacements.title: Read quality signals within their measured scope
replacements.objective: Explain a score using its evidence, coverage, age and limitations.
replacements.content:
A quality badge summarizes stored validation evidence for an item. It is useful for finding evaluated templates and deciding what to inspect next. It does not certify that the answer currently displayed in chat is correct.

A result can be Unscored or have no quality badge when the relevant score is unavailable. That is missing evaluation evidence, not a score of zero, a demonstrated failure or a pass. Check whether the intended artifact and configuration have usable validation records before making a quality claim.

Open the available quality details and inspect the underlying validation date, measured inputs, test/check count, repeated runs, model/configuration and failed or skipped checks. A score from a different revision or unrepresentative cases has limited relevance to your task. A stale-plan or regression warning needs investigation even if another historical number looks strong.

Extraction scores combine measured accuracy and consistency, with cross-field results included when available. Sample-size adjustments can reduce a score supported by little data. Workflow scores use their own evaluated checks and results. Do not apply one fixed formula to every kind of item, or treat configured tier thresholds as universal guarantees.

Accuracy means agreement with the saved expected values under the implemented comparison. Consistency means agreement among measured outputs. Neither proves that the expected values were independently correct or that untested document types will work. Review how the test set was established.

Adding representative test cases improves coverage, but it can lower the measured score when those cases expose failures. More verification does not promise a higher score. Investigate the new failures and compare like-for-like cases before attributing a score change to a repair.

The displayed measurement should be traceable to stored validation records. Chat may describe those records or make other claims; compare the actual details rather than assuming the model either knows everything about the score or cannot see any of it. An assistant's assurance is not a substitute for the record.

**Practice:** Explain a high score from a small, old test set to someone considering a new document type. State what the score supports and what still needs testing.

knowledge_check.question: A template has a high historical score. What can you conclude about a new document?

options.text: Every value in the new result is certified correct.
options.explanation: The score covers measured examples, not every future output.

options.text: The tested examples performed well; check relevance, age and the current source-supported result.
options.explanation: Use the signal as scoped evidence rather than a universal guarantee.

options.text: There is no reason to inspect the underlying test cases.
options.explanation: Coverage and expected-value quality determine what the score means.

replacements.title: Verify and finalize useful test cases
replacements.objective: Turn a proposed extraction into source-checked expected values without treating guesses as ground truth.
replacements.content:
Guided verification helps turn an extraction into a reusable test case. The proposal starts a review; it does not make the extracted values correct or save a completed test case by itself.

1. Use the assigned extraction and document. Ask chat to propose a test case, then inspect the opened verification session and its actual source identity.
2. Review every proposed field against the relevant document passage and the field's meaning. A nearby quote or highlight is a navigation aid, not proof that the value answers the field correctly.
3. Approve a value only when supported. Correct a wrong value from the source. If you cannot establish an expected value, leave the uncertainty explicit or skip that field rather than guessing.
4. Resolve all pending fields and finalize the session. Approved and corrected fields become expected values; skipped fields are omitted. Check the saved test case and its included fields.
5. Run extraction validation with the intended saved cases and inspect the actual results. If fields were skipped, record that coverage gap and use a suitable additional case where the source establishes them.
6. Investigate patterns of failure in the extraction definition or context. A model suggestion is a proposed repair; save, execute and measure it before claiming improvement.

Saving another checked test case expands the evidence available for validation; it does not by itself improve the extraction or raise its score. A new case can reveal an error the earlier cases missed. Keep that case and diagnose the failure rather than removing it to restore a higher number.

This review is part of the learner's own source-checking work. It does not require a staff grading queue. Saving a test case or completing formative practice is also separate from demonstrating the module's assessed outcomes.

**Practice:** A session contains four supported values and one unresolved value. Explain what will and will not be tested if the unresolved field is skipped.

knowledge_check.question: What happens to a skipped field when a verification session is finalized?

options.text: Its guessed value becomes ground truth.
options.explanation: Skipping is not approval and must not introduce a guessed expected value.

options.text: It is omitted from the saved expected values, leaving a coverage gap to address.
options.explanation: Only approved and corrected fields with expected values enter the case.

options.text: The system proves it is always optional.
options.explanation: Skipping one unconfirmed value does not redefine the task requirements.

replacements.title: Review evidence, coverage and retesting
replacements.objective: Connect validation terminology to a defensible decision about a real run.
replacements.content:
**Validation plan:** saved checks that define expected behavior. A plan must match the current workflow and be applied to actual results; saving it does not validate every future run.

**Expected value:** a source-checked answer for a particular case and field. Model-proposed values require review. A skipped or unconfirmed field is not verified ground truth.

**Accuracy and consistency:** agreement with expectations and agreement across repeated outputs. Consistently wrong output remains wrong. Correct shape and nonempty fields are also distinct from correct meaning.

**Representative coverage:** cases that exercise the relevant range of inputs and failures. A fixed number of cases or a high score cannot establish that all important cases are covered. Held-out cases help check whether a repair generalizes beyond the examples used to tune it.

**Validation result and history:** recorded evaluations under particular conditions. Inspect which executions, models, inputs and plan were assessed. A stale plan, unavailable check or old execution limits what the result can establish.

**Repair and regression check:** a documented change followed by new execution and evaluation of both the original failure and other representative cases. Preserve the earlier evidence and explain any test-set changes.

**Review task:** Show one meaningful failure, its source evidence, your saved repair and the linked retest. Explain one remaining coverage limitation. Formative answers and chat assurances do not substitute for that practical evidence.

knowledge_check.question: Which evidence best supports a repair claim?

options.text: A new prompt and an unchanged historical score.
options.explanation: That does not show how the new prompt behaved.

options.text: The original failure, saved change, new linked execution and relevant regression results.
options.explanation: The evidence connects the problem, intervention and measured outcome.

options.text: A model explanation that the change should work.
options.explanation: A predicted improvement is not a measured repair.
